notes: S2-FIX1 T1 (Q2; §5.3, §9.4 case 3): a device key has a valid key-compromise revocation effective at T1; a rotation from that old key to a new key claims T0, before the compromise, and the L0 container has no timestamp evidence at all (so the old key's own declaration is invalid E_KEY_COMPROMISED as well, A1). The rotation's old-key signature fails §9.4 (invalid E_KEY_COMPROMISED), and a signature that fails §9.4 gives another key neither material nor trust: the rotation supplies no new-key material, so a note signed by the new key at T3 is unverifiable E_KEY_UNKNOWN (sigs state unverified). Without this a thief holding the old key could backdate a rotation to a key of their own and sign valid records with it.
